title: Preemptive credit rebalancer for plan lanes and fallback models
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Goal: Implement a preemptive credit rebalancer that proactively adjusts admission probabilities and temporary credit grants across free/paid/enterprise lanes to reduce hard quota failures while preserving latency SLOs and enterprise guarantees. The feature should operate at request admission time and as a periodic background reconciler so that short spikes for free users don't cascade into enterprise degradation, and paid customers receive smooth fairness when credits are transiently depleted.

Requirements:
- Admission controller hook that can temporarily borrow from a short-duration soft-pool when a lane's credit bucket is below threshold. Borrowing must be constrained by plan class and not violate enterprise reserved capacity.
- Circuit-breaker policies to stop borrowing if latency degradation or tail P99 increases beyond configured SLOs.
- Configurable priority decay so older queued requests for higher tiers are handled preferentially without starving free lane throughput entirely.
- Model-fallback integration: when primary model variants behind an enterprise lane are unavailable, the system should route to pre-approved lower-cost quantized variants (or degraded-semantics fallbacks) with explicit tagging in logs and billing flags.
- Observability: per-request trace tags, a simulation dashboard, and synthetic QA harness to validate that rebalancer does not increase 99th percentile latency above threshold.
- Rollout plan: feature-flagged beta, canary at 5% of traffic per-region, gradual scaling to 50% with automatic rollback on error rate or SLO breach.

Acceptance criteria:
1) End-to-end flow (admission -> borrow -> reclaim) validated in integration tests and load tests.
2) No increase > 5% in P99 response time for enterprise tenants in canary runs.
3) Reduction in hard quota rejections for free tier by >= 60% under modeled burst scenarios in the simulation harness.
4) Audit logs showing explicit borrow/grant/reclaim events per request and plan.

Non-goals: this ticket will not change pricing or long-term quota resets; it focuses on short-lived smoothing and graceful degradation only. Longer-term credit market (cross-customer transfer) is out of scope.

notes:
Design decisions: favor ephemeral grants (<=30s) with background reconciler that slowly reclaims credits to avoid oscillation. Use a backoff window per-tenant to limit repeated borrowing. Evaluate telemetry for three signals: credit deficit depth, admission queue length, and recent P99 trend.

Trade-offs considered: 
- Conservative caps vs aggressive smoothing: chose conservative to protect enterprise SLOs.
- In-memory only state vs persisted: persisted to Redis for safety across pod restarts.
- Immediate model fallbacks vs queued retry: prefer immediate fallback to avoid queue piling and to make degraded outputs explicit to downstream apps.
